title: Too expensive and no humain!
body:
I wanted to try this app to help me with my ADHD and I also suffer from depression. I thought it might help me deal with everything that's going on and help me move forward. So I paid for a two-week trial. 

Unfortunately my state of mind was very bad at that time so I didn't use it. I actually opened the app once and my mind was immediately overwhelmed so I never went back. 
It seemed very complicated to me. 

The problem is not there but after the two weeks of trial I tried to cancel so that they don't charge me more time but I couldn't even find where to unsubscribe in the application and saw As I accessed this app through an ad on Facebook (or Instagram), the purchase was not on my "Apple" list (which I didn't know until today). So I thought my purchase would stop there but after 14 days, they charged me almost a hundred dollars for an additional 6 month trial!!! 

I then wrote to them explaining my situation in a very transparent and honest way but I received no kind words or understanding from them. And even though I asked them to cancel this second transaction the same day they charged me! 

They said I didn't cancel before the renewal date even though I did the same day. 

Even after a few email exchanges, they still show no human feeling. 

Thanks to my bank which normally does not reimburse these things but which understood and was lenient given my difficult time. 

Even without my health problem, I think this application is too much expensive.

title: Habio: Where Your Money Checks In But It Never Leaves
body:
If you’re considering downloading Habio, prepare for a journey where your wallet becomes the star of a hostage situation—only, there’s no Liam Neeson coming to save you. I embarked on this misadventure when I downloaded Habio, lured in by its glossy façade and the promise of seamless productivity. Instead, I was greeted by an ensemble of glitches that would make even a beta version blush in embarrassment.

Despite the allure of streamlined interfaces and productivity promises, Habio is less a tool for organization and more a trap for your finances. It’s like buying a first-class ticket on the Titanic purely for the iceberg experience. I attempted to make the best of a sinking situation until the frustration overwhelmed the functionality. When I sought a refund, hoping for some semblance of customer service redemption, I was met with a cold shoulder draped in the fine print of their “terms and conditions.”

The audacity of Habio’s customer service—or should I say, their customer disservice?—is a masterclass in how to alienate users. They hold onto your money with the tenacity of a toddler clutching a favourite toy, making it clear that your financial well-being ranks several leagues below their bottom line.

Let this review serve as a warning: Habio’s real functionality lies in its ability to perform a vanishing act with your cash. Don’t fall for the trap. There are countless other apps and services that actually respect their users and understand the value of customer satisfaction.

title: Do not download this app
body:
Hello, fellow App Store customer.
Read me for some good tea.

I write this review today after a horrendous month of contact with Habio.

I downloaded the app, hopeful and happy. Upon downloading, i realized that it wasn’t really going to help me, so in July 2023, after 1 week, canceled my free trial, I deleted the app, and forgot about it.
I receive a charge (6) months later in February 1st 2024 from habio.
I contact the company, and they respond with “i cancelled too late” - 6 months later? No. I then asked for the specific dates that i allegedly signed up and canceled - with continued emails from them throughout February (6 emails in total) insisting that i had canceled my subscription successfully and would not be further charged, but i was not eligible for a refund.

I suspected this was a scam, since I had not had my phone for 2 months (I am on an island doing scuba training) and i certainly hadn’t had downloaded it again or re subscribed in January or February - simply because i had absolutely no means to.

I submitted a chargeback with my bank after a month, (march 2nd) and on march 5th i got my money back because of my bank <3

I also received an email from habio on march 5th saying that my subscription was NOW cancelled, a month after they said 1) i was already cancelled, and 2) they promised me multiple times in the emails throughout February that i was already cancelled. So, why, pray tell, that I am getting an email on the 5th of march that only NOW my subscription is cancelled?

They want to send out this easy money, and try to make it impossible to get your money back. Stay at them, do not accept no for an answer, and when you have enough evidence, take it to your bank and they will handle the rest for you. Enjoy!
